← Return to Prices

Connect a price source

The Prices screen can check whether the server has an Alpaca configuration. This check reads configuration status only. It does not contact Alpaca or download prices.

Price capture is currently off. A valid API key alone does not make data ready for journal valuation.

What the owner supplies

  1. An Alpaca account with access to the requested historical stock data, and that account’s API key and secret.
  2. A current review of the provider and exchange terms, account entitlement and intended use. Fetching, retaining, displaying and using prices for journal evaluation need the appropriate permissions. Do not assume a free plan covers every operation.
  3. Reviewed security identities, the exchange calendar, raw price and volume basis, and complete corporate-action coverage for the required dates.

Configure server values

An operator can configure ALPACA_API_KEY_ID and ALPACA_API_SECRET_KEY as hosted runtime secrets. The server also expects a current, reviewed ALPACA_DATA_AUTHORIZATION_JSON configuration. Keep credentials out of source files and browser inputs. The source repository’s Alpaca adapter documentation describes the authorization contract.

After configuration, use Check data setup in Prices. “Configuration is present” means its shape and review dates passed the setup checks. The connection, data retrieval and valuation path still need to be verified before capture can be activated.

The owner can also probe the connection. It requests one completed New York day of SPY and reports the outcome without storing anything.

Which prices this adapter supports

The adapter prepares historical, unadjusted US-dollar daily stock bars from the SIP feed. Its conservative completion rule accepts prior New York dates and requires the requested end to be at least 15 minutes old. An October 19 daily bar is therefore deferred until October 20 in New York. These are daily-bar references, not promised auction execution prices.

Each fetched page retains its own response hash and observation time. Incomplete or inconsistent histories remain unavailable. Captured data starts unreviewed; it cannot silently become an eligible stock selection, a paper fill or an actual trade.
